questions.evidence:
A science club makes a shadow log in the schoolyard. Students place one upright stick in a flat patch of ground and mark its position so it will not move. They measure its shadow at nine, eleven, one, and three on a clear day.

The recorded lengths are sixty, thirty-five, thirty, and fifty centimeters. At each check, they also draw an arrow showing which way the shadow points. The teacher asks them to keep the stick and the measuring method the same throughout the activity.

Yuri first writes that the shadow keeps getting shorter all day. Her partner notices the last measurement. Fifty centimeters is longer than thirty, so the sentence does not describe all four observations. Yuri corrects it before handing in the report.

The club plans to repeat the activity on another clear day. They will compare the records without assuming that every date produces exactly the same lengths. Their log describes this stick, this location, and these particular times.
questions.explanation: 須讓敘述符合全部紀錄，避免無限推廣。
options: A description must account for all recorded measurements.
Shadows get shorter at every time of day.
The longest shadow must occur at three.
One measurement predicts all later days exactly.
